free-text-summary-at-root.json.why: The event is closed and has no free-text field, so a summary string at the root is rejected rather than carried off the device (improvement 1, C4).

unrecognized-format-count-not-reported.j.why: When trace_format is unrecognized every token count must be unavailable for reason unrecognized_format, so the console can tell an uncertified harness version from a known format that lacks a class (improvement 5).

evidence-reconciled.json.why: Reconciled evidence comes only from matching provider billing data (6.5), never from a transcript, so a trace event cannot claim it.

hmac-digest-uppercase-hex.json.why: Digests are lowercase hex exactly as the relay writes them; an uppercase digest would never equal the relay's hash, so relay-covered usage would be counted twice (M4).

session-id-with-spaces.json.why: Session IDs use the bounded identifier format with no whitespace, so the field cannot hold prose such as a session title (C4).

token-count-as-float.json.why: Token counts are integers and no JSON under contracts/ may hold a float (6.4).

hmac-algorithm-sha256-unkeyed.json.why: Only HMAC-SHA256 under the per-org key is allowed; an unkeyed SHA-256 of a provider message ID can be recomputed by anyone holding the ID and would not match the relay's keyed hash (improvement 2, M4).

raw-provider-message-id-not-hashed.json.why: The provider message ID leaves the device only as a keyed-hash object, never as the raw ID string (improvement 2).

unavailable-count-given-as-zero.json.why: Unavailable is not zero: an unavailable count must have a null value, so Cursor's hidden reasoning cannot be reported as a measured-looking 0 (6.5, improvement 4).
